items.label: Endpoints do not return listed fields
items.description: Reports db.query, db.get, db.add, db.edit, db.patch and db.add_or_edit statements whose output list returns a listed or schema-sensitive field of their table. Inspects the db statement's output list (output = ["id", "name"]), not a response assembled by hand; an absent or default output returns every field and is reported when the table has a forbidden field. Every nesting depth of the object's stack is inspected, and a dotted entry reaches inside a paged result (items.email). A field is only forbidden on a table that has it, and an output entry is attributed only through the statement's own declarations: a field of its own table, its own or a declared join alias as a prefix (user.email), or a literal eval alias; table.field restricts a name to that table. An entry whose provenance cannot be resolved (a runtime value, a computed eval, an undeclared prefix) is not reported, and count, exists and aggregate queries return no record. Narrow the objects with the shared scope params.

goals.goal: Endpoints require login
goals.summary: Every endpoint requires authentication, unless it or its API group is tagged public.
goals.limits: Checks the endpoint's saved authentication setting; what a logged-in caller is then allowed to do is not evaluated.

goals.goal: Endpoints don't return personal data
goals.summary: Endpoints never return the personal-data fields you list, or any field marked sensitive in its table's schema.
goals.limits: Reads the output list of each database statement; a response assembled by hand or a value passed back through a function is not inspected.

goals.goal: Users only reach their own records
goals.summary: Reads of owned tables filter on the owner field against the logged-in user, and new records take their owner from the login rather than the request.
goals.limits: Confirms the filter is written on the read, not that it holds on every branch; an owner check done in a called function or after the read is not seen.

rules.title: Reads filter on the logged-in user
New records take their owner from the login, not the request

goals.goal: No secrets are hardcoded
goals.summary: API keys, tokens, private keys and credentialed URLs are never written as literals in function stacks or agent settings; they belong in environment variables.
goals.limits: Recognizes the built-in credential shapes only; a secret in a format of your own is not matched.

goals.goal: Data only goes to approved vendors
goals.summary: Outbound requests, cloud and email providers and AI model providers are limited to the vendors you approve.
goals.limits: A destination built at run time is reported as unresolved rather than checked, and what is sent to an approved vendor is not inspected.

goals.goal: Users can't make themselves admin
goals.summary: Record creates and edits never take a privilege field such as role or is_admin straight from request input.
goals.limits: Covers db.add and db.edit, so add a rule for any other write statement you use such as db.patch; a value copied into a variable before the write is not traced.

rules.title: New records do not take privilege fields from the request
Edits do not take privilege fields from the request

goals.goal: Public endpoints can't change data
goals.summary: An endpoint that requires no authentication never changes or deletes records.
goals.limits: Inspects the endpoint's own stack, including nested branches; a write inside a called function is not followed.

rules.title: Public endpoints do not change or delete records

goals.goal: Admin endpoints check the caller's role
goals.summary: Every endpoint tagged admin calls your role-check function as its first statement, passing the logged-in user.
goals.limits: Confirms the call is written first, not what the function decides; an endpoint missing the admin tag is not examined.

rules.title: Admin endpoints call the role check first

goals.goal: No table truncation or raw SQL
goals.summary: No function stack truncates a table or runs a direct SQL query.
goals.limits: Matches the statements by name wherever they appear; SQL sent to an external database uses different statements, which you can add to the list.

rules.title: Truncation and raw SQL stay out

goals.goal: External requests verify TLS certificates
goals.summary: Every external request verifies the TLS certificate of the server it talks to.
goals.limits: Reads the literal setting on each request; a value computed at run time is reported as unverifiable.

rules.title: Requests verify TLS peers

goals.goal: Login tokens expire within an hour
goals.summary: Every authentication token expires within one hour of being created.
goals.limits: Reads the literal expiration on each token statement; a value computed at run time is reported as unverifiable.

rules.title: Tokens expire within one hour

goals.goal: Endpoints are tested
goals.summary: Every endpoint is called by a workflow test, and every protected endpoint has a test asserting that an anonymous call is rejected.
goals.limits: Inspects test definitions without running them, so a test that exists but fails still counts as coverage.

goals.goal: Sensitive tables are only reached by logged-in endpoints
goals.summary: Every endpoint that reaches a table carrying your sensitive-data tag, directly or through a function, requires authentication.
goals.limits: Depends on the tables being tagged, and reaches tables through called functions but through addons only when follow_addons is on.

rules.title: Endpoints reaching sensitive tables require login

goals.goal: Sensitive fields are marked sensitive
goals.summary: The fields you list are marked sensitive wherever a table declares them.
goals.limits: Reads the table schemas only; a field holding personal data under a name you did not list is not found.

rules.title: Listed fields are marked sensitive

goals.goal: Tables holding confidential data are tagged
goals.summary: A table with a text field you list, such as notes, carries the confidential tag.
goals.limits: Matches fields by exact name and type; a table holding the same data under another field name is not found.

goals.goal: Saved views hide sensitive fields
goals.summary: Every saved table view hides the fields marked sensitive in its table's schema.
goals.limits: Depends on fields being marked sensitive in the schema; a table without saved views passes.

goals.goal: Logs don't contain request, user or secret data
goals.summary: Debug logs never reference request input, the logged-in user or environment variables.
goals.limits: Inspects the log value as written; data copied into a variable first and then logged is not traced.

rules.title: Logs name events, not input, auth or env

goals.goal: External calls handle their own failures
goals.summary: Every external request sits inside error handling, so a vendor failure is handled rather than raised.
goals.limits: Confirms the request sits inside a try_catch at some depth, not that every path through the catch handles the failure.

rules.title: Requests sit inside a try_catch

goals.goal: Middleware doesn't swallow errors
goals.summary: No middleware is set to swallow the exceptions it catches.
goals.limits: Reads each middleware's saved exception setting; what the middleware does with an error it surfaces is not evaluated.

rules.title: Middleware surfaces the exceptions it catches

goals.goal: External requests set a timeout
goals.summary: Every external request sets an explicit timeout, so one slow vendor cannot stall a workspace.
goals.limits: Confirms a timeout is written on each request, not that its value is short enough.

rules.title: Requests declare a timeout

goals.goal: GET endpoints only read
goals.summary: A GET endpoint only reads data; every write sits behind a verb that says so.
goals.limits: Inspects the endpoint's own stack, including nested branches; a write inside a called function is not followed.

rules.title: GET endpoints only read

goals.goal: Endpoints check the caller before writing
goals.summary: Every authenticated endpoint that writes records checks the logged-in user with a precondition first.
goals.limits: Reads the top-level stack only; a check inside a called function or a nested branch is not seen.

rules.title: A permission check precedes each write

goals.goal: Endpoint inputs are typed and bounded
goals.summary: Endpoint inputs declare suitable types and page-size limits, personal data stays out of URL paths, and every declared input is used.
goals.limits: Reads the declared inputs and the endpoint's stack; validation done inside a called function is not seen.

goals.goal: Protected endpoints run your auth middleware
goals.summary: Every endpoint that requires authentication runs the middleware you name.
goals.limits: Confirms the middleware is attached and active, not what it does.

rules.title: Protected endpoints attach the middleware

goals.goal: Users sign in through one auth table
goals.summary: The workspace has exactly one auth table, and every authenticated endpoint uses it.
goals.limits: Counts auth-enabled tables across the whole branch; several intentional auth tables mean this goal does not fit.

goals.goal: Only the audit function writes the audit log
goals.summary: The audit log table exists, and only the function you name writes to it.
goals.limits: Checks where each write is defined; a caller can still use the approved function to write whatever it passes in.

rules.title: The audit log table exists
Only the audit function writes it

goals.goal: Retained data has a cleanup task
goals.summary: Every table carrying your retained-data tag is referenced by a scheduled task that cleans it up.
goals.limits: Confirms a task references the table, not that it deletes the right records or runs on schedule.

rules.title: Retained tables have a cleanup task

goals.goal: Table triggers don't write their own table
goals.summary: A table trigger never writes to its own table, so a change cannot feed itself.
goals.limits: Inspects the trigger's own stack; a write inside a called function is not followed.
